summary: Reproduced PR 2799's concrete MI350X regressions against PR 2736 at 21e526df7844155adec0c2163992178bf899ba99, then added a pre-deduplication top-k-size gate that preserves the beneficial compact path while avoiding expensive torch.unique work for the reviewed large-query cases.

tests.what_was_measured: MI355X warmed median latency and peak GPU allocation. Reproduced 64-query selective slowdown at 1.519x and 256/1024-query late-fallback slowdowns at 1.993x/2.291x with 166724096/213910016-byte peaks.
Four GPU tests passed: independent FP8 dequant reference, physical alias dedup/remap, small-prefix fallback, new pre-dedup large-top-k fallback, and invalid sentinels.
The 64/256/1024-query counterexamples chose early full fallback, used exactly the full path's 150994944-byte peak, and measured 0.795x/0.802x/0.827x of the separately warmed full baseline.
Preserved beneficial compact behavior: 262144 logical rows reduced to 4029 rows, 301989888 to 4641408 BF16 bytes, and 0.6235 ms to 0.2494 ms (2.500x).
Repository formatting, lint, spelling, syntax, registered-test taxonomy, and policy hooks all passed.
On ROCm, 1 passed, 4 skipped, and 2 subtests stopped before attention because the fixture page size is 64 while the available legacy HIP DSA path requires page size 1.

gpu_evidence: All focused numerical and performance checks executed checked-out source on one AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2.
remaining_limitations: BF16 flashmla_sparse attention output and end-to-end sparse-prefill performance remain unverified because the assigned AMD MI355X is not the required NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell architecture.
The ROCm DSA backend fixture cannot reach attention with page size 64 on the available legacy HIP path, which requires page size 1.
No native C++, CUDA, HIP, or FlyDSL source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
